intervals.note: 2015 is a lower bound only (the year INSPIRE's CTA experiment record was created); no fetched source this session gives a construction-start date, a completion date, or a per-site percentage. CTAO's own wording implies construction and (partial) operation are concurrent, similar to how LST-1 and some MSTs are already reported elsewhere to be taking data on La Palma while the observatory as a whole is not complete. Status is kept at 'construction' pending a source that states otherwise.

intervals.label: LST sub-array (LST-1 to LST-4, CTAO-North) completed and inaugurated
intervals.note: Added 2026-10-25. CTAO press release, La Palma, 15 October 2026: 250 scientists "celebrated the inauguration of the Large-Sized Telescope (LST) sub-array at the CTAO-North site"; "The completion of the four telescopes marks a significant milestone ... and represents a crucial step toward the full scientific operation" of CTAO; "With the three new LSTs (LST-2, LST-3, and LST-4) joining the existing LST-1, the four telescopes will become a true array"; "Over the coming years, the LSTs will undergo commissioning and integration into CTAO operations." LST-1, the prototype, has been observing 'even during its commissioning phase' since 2020. Recorded as a milestone annotation (kind phase) and not as a commissioning interval: the Atlas holds one aggregate record for the whole observatory (both sites, all telescope classes), not one per telescope, the article gives no commissioning dates for LST-2 to LST-4 and says commissioning is still ahead, and the rest of CTAO (MSTs, SSTs, CTAO-South) remains under construction. The observatory-level status stays `construction`.

summary.plain: A next-generation gamma-ray observatory being built at two sites, one in Spain and one in Chile, using dozens of telescopes of three different sizes to see the whole sky and the widest range of gamma-ray energies of any single project.
summary.technical: Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory: two-site (La Palma, Spain / Paranal, Chile) imaging-atmospheric-Cherenkov array using Large-, Medium- and Small-Sized Telescope classes (up to 4 LST + 23 MST north, up to 23 MST + 37 SST south, per the observatory's own technology page) to cover 20 GeV-300 TeV. Headquarters in Bologna, Italy; Science Data Management Centre in Zeuthen, Germany. Under construction as of the sources fetched this session.

unique_capabilities.value: The next-generation ground-based gamma-ray observatory: two array sites (Northern and Southern Hemisphere) using three telescope size classes (Large, Medium and Small) to cover the widest energy range of any single gamma-ray facility, 20 GeV to 300 TeV.
